Nuclear Physics Angular Momentum Coupling Guide

This document provides the theoretical background and practical usage guide for the angular_momentum_coupling.py utility. This tool calculates allowed final nuclear states based on quantum mechanical selection rules.

1. Theoretical Basis

The code implements the Channel Spin Coupling Scheme, which is a standard method for determining angular momentum conservation in nuclear reactions.

Conservation Laws

In any nuclear reaction Target+Particle→Final_StateTarget + Particle \to Final\_StateTarget+Particle→Final_State, the following quantities are conserved:

  1. Total Angular Momentum (J⃗\vec{J}J):

    J⃗final=J⃗target+s⃗particle+ℓ⃗\vec{J}_{final} = \vec{J}_{target} + \vec{s}_{particle} + \vec{\ell}Jfinal​=Jtarget​+sparticle​+ℓ

  2. Parity (π\piπ):

    πfinal=πtarget×πparticle×(−1)ℓ\pi_{final} = \pi_{target} \times \pi_{particle} \times (-1)^{\ell}πfinal​=πtarget​×πparticle​×(−1)ℓ

Where:

  • J⃗target\vec{J}_{target}Jtarget​: Spin of the target nucleus.
  • s⃗particle\vec{s}_{particle}sparticle​: Intrinsic spin of the interacting particle (projectile or transferred cluster).
  • ℓ⃗\vec{\ell}ℓ: Relative orbital angular momentum between the target and the particle.

Coupling Scheme Used in Code

The code performs the vector addition in two steps (Channel Spin representation):

  1. Calculate Channel Spin (S⃗\vec{S}S): Couples the target spin and particle spin.

    S⃗=J⃗target+s⃗particle\vec{S} = \vec{J}_{target} + \vec{s}_{particle}S=Jtarget​+sparticle​

    Possible values: ∣Jtarget−sparticle∣≤S≤Jtarget+sparticle|J_{target} - s_{particle}| \le S \le J_{target} + s_{particle}∣Jtarget​−sparticle​∣≤S≤Jtarget​+sparticle​

  2. Calculate Final Spin (J⃗final\vec{J}_{final}Jfinal​): Couples the channel spin with the orbital angular momentum.

    J⃗final=S⃗+ℓ⃗\vec{J}_{final} = \vec{S} + \vec{\ell}Jfinal​=S+ℓ

    Possible values: ∣S−ℓ∣≤Jfinal≤S+ℓ|S - \ell| \le J_{final} \le S + \ell∣S−ℓ∣≤Jfinal​≤S+ℓ

2. Application to Different Reaction Types

To use the code correctly, you must identify the correct "Particle" input based on the reaction mechanism.

A. Resonance and Capture Reactions

Examples: (p, γ), (n, γ), (p, p')

In these reactions, a projectile fuses with the target to form a compound nucleus (resonance).

  • Target Input: Spin/Parity of the target nucleus.
  • Particle Input: Spin/Parity of the projectile.

B. Single-Nucleon Transfer Reactions

Examples: (d,p)(d, p)(d,p), (p,d)(p, d)(p,d), (3He,d)(^3\text{He}, d)(3He,d), (α,t)(\alpha, t)(α,t)

In these reactions, a single nucleon is transferred between the projectile and the target. You must input the properties of the transferred nucleon, not the beam.

  • Target Input: Spin/Parity of the target nucleus.
  • Particle Input: Spin/Parity of the transferred nucleon (nnn or ppp).

Note on j-transfer: In transfer physics, we often discuss the transferred total angular momentum j (where j⃗=ℓ⃗+s⃗\vec{j} = \vec{\ell} + \vec{s}j​=ℓ+s). The code lists results by Channel Spin S. The set of allowed final JπJ^\piJπ values is identical regardless of the coupling order.

C. Two-Nucleon Transfer Reactions

Examples: (p,t)(p, t)(p,t), (t,p)(t, p)(t,p), (3He,n)(^3\text{He}, n)(3He,n), (α,d)(\alpha, d)(α,d)

In these reactions, a pair of nucleons is transferred. The total spin of this pair depends on the coupling of the two nucleons.

1. Identical Nucleon Transfer (2n or 2p)

Reactions: (p,t)(p, t)(p,t), (t,p)(t, p)(t,p) (2n transfer); (3He,n)(^3\text{He}, n)(3He,n) (2p transfer)

For the transfer of two identical nucleons (2n or 2p) in the same shell model orbit, the Pauli Exclusion Principle dictates that their total wavefunction must be antisymmetric.

  • If they are in a relative s-state (spatially symmetric, L=0L=0L=0), their spin wavefunction must be antisymmetric.

  • An antisymmetric spin state for two fermions corresponds to a Singlet State (S=0S=0S=0).

  • ENSDF Policy: For (p,t)(p, t)(p,t), (t,p)(t, p)(t,p), and (3He,n)(^3\text{He}, n)(3He,n) reactions, it is standard to assume the transferred pair is in an anti-parallel spin state (S=0S=0S=0).

  • Particle Input: 0+

2. Neutron-Proton Transfer (1n1p)

Reactions: (α,d)(\alpha, d)(α,d), (d,α)(d, \alpha)(d,α), (3He,p)(^3\text{He}, p)(3He,p), (p,3He)(p, ^3\text{He})(p,3He)

For the transfer of a neutron-proton pair, the selection rules depend on the projectile/ejectile properties.

  • (α,d)(\alpha, d)(α,d) and (d,α)(d, \alpha)(d,α):

    • Both ddd and α\alphaα have T=0T=0T=0. Thus, only T=0T=0T=0 transfer is allowed.
    • Antisymmetry requires S+TS+TS+T to be odd (for relative L=0L=0L=0). Since T=0T=0T=0, the transfer is restricted to S=1S=1S=1 (spin triplet).
    • Particle Input: 1+

  • (3He,p)(^3\text{He}, p)(3He,p) and (p,3He)(p, ^3\text{He})(p,3He):

    • Both particles have S=1/2,T=1/2S=1/2, T=1/2S=1/2,T=1/2.
    • Allowed transfers are (S=0,T=1)(S=0, T=1)(S=0,T=1) and (S=1,T=0)(S=1, T=0)(S=1,T=0).
    • Particle Input:
      • For S=0S=0S=0 component: 0+
      • For S=1S=1S=1 component: 1+
    • Note: Both components often contribute.

D. Cluster Transfer Reactions

Examples: (6Li,d)(^6\text{Li}, d)(6Li,d), (7Li,t)(^7\text{Li}, t)(7Li,t)

An alpha particle (or other cluster) is transferred.

  • Target Input: Spin/Parity of the target nucleus.
  • Particle Input: Spin/Parity of the transferred cluster.

E. Alpha Inelastic Scattering

Examples: (α,α′)(\alpha, \alpha')(α,α′)

In inelastic scattering, the target nucleus is excited to a higher energy state.

  • (α,α′)(\alpha, \alpha')(α,α′): The alpha particle has spin 0. Since the projectile spin cannot flip, the angular momentum transfer is purely orbital (ℓ⃗\vec{\ell}ℓ). This selectively excites Natural Parity states (π=(−1)ℓ\pi = (-1)^\ellπ=(−1)ℓ).

  • Particle Input: 0+

    • Note: This treats the angular momentum transfer as a spin-0 boson transfer.

3. Interpreting the Output

When you run the code:

python .github/scripts/angular_momentum_coupling.py 3/2- 1/2+

You receive output like:

Target: J=3/2 π=- | Particle: s=1/2 π=+
Channel Spins S: 1, 2: from |3/2 - 1/2| to 3/2 + 1/2
------------------------------------------------------------
L   Wave  Parity   s     Final Jπ
------------------------------------------------------------
0   s     -        1     1-
0   s     -        2     2-
------------------------------------------------------------
1   p     +        1     0+, 1+, 2+
1   p     +        2     1+, 2+, 3+
------------------------------------------------------------
  • L (Wave): The orbital angular momentum (ℓ\ellℓ) between target and particle, ranging from 0 to 4 in the output (s, p, d, f, g waves).
  • Parity: The parity of the final state, determined by πfinal=πtarget×πparticle×(−1)ℓ\pi_{final} = \pi_{target} \times \pi_{particle} \times (-1)^{\ell}πfinal​=πtarget​×πparticle​×(−1)ℓ.
  • s (Channel Spin): The intermediate coupling S=J⃗target+s⃗particleS = \vec{J}_{target} + \vec{s}_{particle}S=Jtarget​+sparticle​ before adding orbital angular momentum.
    • For 3/2−3/2^-3/2− target and 1/2+1/2^+1/2+ particle: SSS ranges from ∣3/2−1/2∣=1|3/2 - 1/2| = 1∣3/2−1/2∣=1 to 3/2+1/2=23/2 + 1/2 = 23/2+1/2=2.
  • Final Jπ: All allowed total angular momentum and parity combinations for each (L,S)(L, S)(L,S) pair, calculated from ∣S−ℓ∣≤Jfinal≤S+ℓ|S - \ell| \le J_{final} \le S + \ell∣S−ℓ∣≤Jfinal​≤S+ℓ.

Example Analysis: 59Cu(p,γ)60Zn^{59}\text{Cu}(p, \gamma)^{60}\text{Zn}59Cu(p,γ)60Zn

  • Target: 59Cu^{59}\text{Cu}59Cu (3/2−3/2^-3/2−)
  • Particle: Proton (1/2+1/2^+1/2+)
  • Channel Spins: S=1,2S = 1, 2S=1,2 (from ∣3/2−1/2∣|3/2 - 1/2|∣3/2−1/2∣ to 3/2+1/23/2 + 1/23/2+1/2)
  • Results:
    • s-wave capture (L=0L=0L=0): Parity = (−)×(+)×(−1)0=−(-) \times (+) \times (-1)^0 = -(−)×(+)×(−1)0=−
      • S=1S=1S=1: Jπ=1−J^\pi = 1^-Jπ=1−
      • S=2S=2S=2: Jπ=2−J^\pi = 2^-Jπ=2−
    • p-wave capture (L=1L=1L=1): Parity = (−)×(+)×(−1)1=+(-) \times (+) \times (-1)^1 = +(−)×(+)×(−1)1=+
      • S=1S=1S=1: Jπ=0+,1+,2+J^\pi = 0^+, 1^+, 2^+Jπ=0+,1+,2+ (from ∣1−1∣|1-1|∣1−1∣ to 1+11+11+1)
      • S=2S=2S=2: Jπ=1+,2+,3+J^\pi = 1^+, 2^+, 3^+Jπ=1+,2+,3+ (from ∣2−1∣|2-1|∣2−1∣ to 2+12+12+1)
    • d-wave capture (L=2L=2L=2): Parity = −-−
      • S=1S=1S=1: Jπ=1−,2−,3−J^\pi = 1^-, 2^-, 3^-Jπ=1−,2−,3−
      • S=2S=2S=2: Jπ=0−,1−,2−,3−,4−J^\pi = 0^-, 1^-, 2^-, 3^-, 4^-Jπ=0−,1−,2−,3−,4−

4. Isospin Coupling

For transfer reactions, isospin (TTT) provides additional selection rules.

  • Single Nucleon Transfer: Transferring one nucleon (nnn or ppp) changes isospin by Ttransfer=1/2T_{transfer} = 1/2Ttransfer​=1/2.
  • Identical Nucleon Pair (2n/2p): In a relative L=0L=0L=0 state, the Pauli Principle requires S=0S=0S=0 (spin singlet) and T=1T=1T=1 (isospin triplet). Thus Ttransfer=1T_{transfer} = 1Ttransfer​=1.
  • Neutron-Proton Pair (np):
    • Deuteron-like (S=1,T=0S=1, T=0S=1,T=0): Ttransfer=0T_{transfer} = 0Ttransfer​=0
    • Singlet (S=0,T=1S=0, T=1S=0,T=1): Ttransfer=1T_{transfer} = 1Ttransfer​=1

Selection Rule: The final isospin is determined by vector addition:

T⃗f=T⃗target+T⃗transfer\vec{T}_f = \vec{T}_{target} + \vec{T}_{transfer}Tf​=Ttarget​+Ttransfer​

Note: This tool calculates angular momentum (JπJ^\piJπ) only. Isospin selection rules must be applied separately.
